title: A School Leader's Letter to Parents: It's Time to Address Our School's Use of Social Media
author: Emily Cherkin
summary: Cherkin publishes, with her own framing, a letter from Dr. Pesha Kletenik, head of Manhattan Day School, announcing that the school will stop posting clear, identifiable images of students' faces on its public social media accounts as part of becoming the first school designated 'Tech-Intentional' by Cherkin's certification process. The letter explains that the designation followed three years of work examining educational technology use and personal device policy at the school, including removing 1:1 issued iPads and Chromebooks. Kletenik frames the new social media policy as both a safety measure and a values statement: if the school is asking students to be thoughtful about their digital lives, the institution should model that same intentionality rather than exempting itself. The school will replace public social posts of children's faces with a private, parent-only photo gallery, preserving family visibility into school life without creating a public digital footprint for students who never consented to it.
points: The letter's framing of the policy as 'both a safety measure and a statement of our values' explicitly ties institutional social-media practice to the school's broader tech-intentional pedagogy, rather than treating privacy protection and educational technology policy as separate issues.

Replacing public-facing student photos with a private, parent-only photo gallery is offered as a concrete way to preserve family visibility into school life without creating the public digital footprint that concerns the policy addresses — a specific operational compromise, not just a restriction.

The line 'if we are asking our children to be thoughtful about their digital lives, we believe we should model that same intentionality as a school' makes institutional modeling of digital behavior an explicit accountability standard for the school itself, not just its students.

The designation process is described as a three-year effort that already included removing 1:1 issued devices, situating the social media policy as one deliberate step within a sustained, multi-year institutional program rather than a reactive one-off decision.
quotes: As you may have seen, MDS is honored to be the first school in the nation to be designated "Tech-Intentional®" by leading expert and author Emily Cherkin. This recognition is the culmination of three years of thoughtful and intensive work examining our practices around technology.

We view this designation not as a final achievement, but as an ongoing commitment. Becoming Tech-Intentional® does not mean rejecting technology. Rather, it means being intentional about when, why, and how we use it, grounded in research about child development, learning, and well-being.

Moving forward, we will not post clear images of students' faces or other recognizable identifying information on our public social media accounts. Our public social media platforms will continue to highlight the wonderful work of our school and serve as an important way to tell the MDS story.

This decision is both a safety measure and a statement of our values. If we are asking our children to be thoughtful about their digital lives, we believe we should model that same intentionality as a school.
Our children deserve an environment in which their privacy is protected and their digital footprints are created thoughtfully and with care.

At the same time, we want our families to continue seeing and celebrating the wonderful things happening at MDS! Our new MDS 2026-27 Parent Photo Gallery will be regularly updated with photos from events, programs, and special moments throughout the year.
